meta.topic: Two banking systems show different balances

problem:
A customer of Meridian Bank checks the mobile app and sees a balance of EUR 4,120, then calls the contact centre, where the agent's screen shows EUR 3,850. The difference is EUR 270, exactly the amount of a card payment the customer made that morning. The customer believes the bank has taken money twice, and the agent cannot say which balance is right.

The two systems are showing different views of the same account at different points in the posting sequence. The mobile app may show the available balance after a pending authorisation, while the agent screen may show the ledger balance before the clearing record arrived, or one system may be reading stale replicated data. The learner must trace the source of truth, the posting sequence, pending entries and replication, and explain the difference without guessing.
solution:
Start by defining what each balance means. The ledger balance is the posted balance in the core banking system, and it is authoritative for posted funds. The available balance is the ledger balance less pending authorisations and holds, and it is authoritative for what the customer can spend. A channel balance may be either of these, or a cached copy of one of them, and the screen must say which one it shows.

Trace the EUR 270 payment through its full sequence. The card authorisation places a hold and reduces the available balance immediately, but it does not change the ledger balance until clearing posts the charge. If the mobile app shows the available balance and the agent screen shows the ledger balance, a EUR 270 difference is expected and correct, and the explanation is the pending authorisation, not an error. If both screens claim to show the same balance type, check replication: when was each copy last updated, did the posting event reach both systems, and is one system reading a stale cache?

Check the identifiers as well. An internal transaction ID reused with a different meaning can map the EUR 270 to the wrong account or the wrong payment, so confirm that the instruction ID, end-to-end ID and posting reference all point to the same transaction. If the difference is a genuine data defect, correct it once through a controlled process with an audit trail, and fix the replication or caching cause. If the difference is a timing or definition difference, explain it plainly to the customer and record the explanation against the case.

decision.question: The mobile app shows EUR 4,120 and the contact centre screen shows EUR 3,850 for the same account, a difference of EUR 270 matching a card payment made that morning. What should the analyst do first?

options.label: A
options.detail: Tell the customer to check again tomorrow.

options.label: B
options.detail: Tell the customer the higher balance is correct.

options.label: C
options.detail: Adjust one system to match the other.

options.label: D
options.detail: Identify which system is authoritative for each balance type, trace the EUR 270 payment through authorisation, posting and replication, and compare the same account at the same point in time.

decisionRationale: Option D is correct because the two screens may show different balance types or different points in time, and only tracing the payment and naming the authoritative source can say which value is right. Option B picks a value without evidence. Option C changes data to hide the difference. Option A leaves the customer without an answer.

steps.title: Makes a EUR 270 card payment in the morning
Authorises the payment and places a hold on the available balance
Shows the available balance of EUR 4,120 after the hold
Shows the ledger balance of EUR 3,850 on the agent screen
Identifies the balance type each screen shows and the authoritative source for each
Traces the EUR 270 payment by its references through authorisation, clearing and replication
Determines whether the difference is a pending hold, a replication lag or a genuine defect
Explains the correct balance to the customer, or corrects the defect once with an audit trail

happy: The analyst finds the mobile app shows the available balance after the EUR 270 authorisation hold, while the agent screen shows the ledger balance before clearing. Both values are correct for their own definition. The customer receives a clear explanation, the clearing record posts later that day, both balances converge, and no correction is needed.

negative.title: Stale replicated data
negative.detail: One system reads a cached balance that has not been updated since the payment posted. Check the replication timestamp and the last event applied. Refresh the cache from the authoritative source and fix the replication lag.

negative.title: Missing ledger posting
negative.detail: The payment cleared but the ledger posting is missing, so the ledger balance is wrong. Reconcile the payment engine against the ledger, replay the posting once with the original reference, and alert on the gap.

negative.title: Identifier mapped to the wrong meaning
negative.detail: An internal ID is reused as the end-to-end reference, so the payment is matched to the wrong record. Maintain separate fields for internal ID, instruction ID, end-to-end ID and posting reference, and re-map the affected records correctly.

negative.title: Report totals wrong, source correct
negative.detail: A management report shows a different balance from the operational screens. Trace lineage from the source through extraction and aggregation, reconcile control totals at each stage, and fix the stage that caused the variance.

technical: Name the authoritative source for each data item: the core ledger for posted balances, the authorisation system for holds, and the payment engine for payment state. Define the balance types explicitly and label every screen with the type it shows. Record the posting sequence with timestamps so any two views can be compared at the same point in time. Use versioned, idempotent events for replication, and record the last applied event and timestamp on each replica so staleness is visible. Keep instruction ID, end-to-end ID, transaction ID and posting reference in separate fields with a documented meaning. Mask sensitive data in logs and support screens, and log every correction with its reason, approver and original values.

messages.title: Bank-to-customer statement showing the posted ledger balance and entries.
Bank-to-customer debit or credit notification for an individual posting.
Payment status report used to confirm the payment state behind a balance difference.
Issuer decision that places the hold behind an available-balance difference.

accounting: The ledger balance is the accounting truth for posted funds, and the available balance is the ledger balance less pending holds. No balance may be adjusted to match another screen; a genuine defect is corrected once through a controlled process with a reason, an approver and an audit trail. Pending authorisations sit as holds, not as postings, and they expire under the agreed rules if clearing never arrives. Reconciliation between the ledger, the authorisation system and the channel balances runs on a scheduled cycle, and differences beyond tolerance go to a worklist with an owner and an ageing rule. Customer complaints about balances are answered with the specific payment, its state and its timestamp, not with a general assurance.

scenarios.when: an older event arrives after a newer state
scenarios.then: the payment state does not regress.

scenarios.given: an instruction ID and end-to-end ID are both supplied
scenarios.then: each is placed in its correct semantic field.

scenarios.given: source transactions reconcile but report totals do not
scenarios.then: the stage causing the variance is identified with reproducible evidence.

questions.question: What is the difference between a ledger balance and an available balance?
options: The available balance is always higher.
The ledger balance is the posted balance; the available balance is the ledger balance less pending authorisations and holds.
The ledger balance includes future payments.
questions.explanation: A pending authorisation reduces what the customer can spend without yet changing the posted ledger balance.

questions.question: Two systems show different balances for the same account. What is the first question to ask?
options: Which system does the customer prefer?
Which balance type does each screen show, and which system is authoritative for it?
questions.explanation: Different balance types and different update times explain most differences. The authoritative source must be named before any value is judged.

questions.question: A replica shows a stale balance. How is staleness detected?
options: By checking the replication timestamp and the last event applied against the authoritative source.
By comparing it to another replica.
questions.explanation: A replica should record when it was last updated and which event it last applied, so lag is visible and measurable.

questions.question: A genuine balance defect is found. How should it be corrected?
options: By asking the customer to ignore it.
By editing the screen to show the right number.
By posting an offsetting entry without a reason.
Once, through a controlled correction process with a reason, an approver and an audit trail, and by fixing the underlying cause.
questions.explanation: Corrections need a recorded reason and approval, and the cause must be fixed so the defect does not return.
